notes: DS-GEN-18 STALLED's own corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which breaches the mechanical bar the brief itself enforces (no semicolon); per the brief's own rule not to imitate a corpus breach, I wrote a fresh two-sentence spine instead of copying it verbatim.
DS-ECO-1 COMBINATION C3's corpus line uses a colon, which PART V of the brief lists as a device the fair copy does not have (notebook-only); avoided it in my own version for the same reason.

Two stance values in the turn ("threshold" on PRESSURED, "counterforce" on TIER: minor shadow activity) are not among the brief's three defined stances (ledger/street/visitor), so their intended effect on the prose beyond a flavor tag was unclear.

DS-ECO-9 PRESSURED instructs writing exactly one sentence and no second, but its own corpus fallback is two sentences -- a direct contradiction between the card's instruction and the fallback it supplies. I followed the one-sentence instruction.

DS-ECO-12 INCOME MIX's pool title says "two or three sources between them" but the field data given is economicState.incomeSources.length = 10 (not marked UNREADABLE the way other engine-decided fields are); unclear whether "two or three" or the length of 10 is authoritative, so I asserted no specific count either way.

The `stance` label on each pool (visitor / street / ledger / threshold / counterforce) is given but the brief only says the three old stances survive as 'the spine line's tag', and 'threshold' and 'counterforce' are not among them (ledger/street/visitor). With faces:0 everywhere, it was unclear whether a stance is supposed to shape the bare spine at all, so I wrote all spines as the archiver's bare fact per ruling 40 and the SHAPE-OF-WHAT-YOU-RETURN section.

Two corpus lines break bars the brief declares hard, and the brief says to keep the CLAIM but not imitate the breach — leaving the claim itself unusable in one case. DS-ECO-6's corpus asserts 'nothing organised behind it', which the brief's own floor-1 example names as refused on a town whose rows list a street gang and front businesses, and this town lists both. I kept the 'minor' reading and dropped the 'nothing organised' claim; if the corpus claim is mandatory, that pool is unwritable.

The 'second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' rule collides with pools whose only fields are 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD' (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18). There is no lawful second sentence available there, which is not stated; I wrote one sentence in each. Similarly DS-ECO-12's INCOME MIX key says 'two or three sources between them' while the field reads a length of ten, so the key and the field disagree and no digit may be written either way.

The dm-only pool (DS-ECO-6) says the private note 'still rides in `spine`' and that `notebook` is none, so the schema's notebook array is empty on the one unit that is actually a notebook entry. That is internally consistent but inverts the audience rule stated in the brief's DM REGISTER section, which says notebook carries the private rows on audience dm.

Slot guidance is permissive ('slots you may use') with no instruction on whether an offered slot must appear. Four pools offer {settlement}, but the page-level bar allows the name at most once per unit and never as the first word of two units, so I spent it once, mid-sentence, and wrote around it elsewhere. Whether an unused slot counts against the unit is not said.

Page is audience dm, but every one of the 17 pools says 'faces to write: 0' and 'notebook: none'. So the whole DM register (PART V) and the entire face machinery of the brief (sources, pairs, weighings, compromised roles, one face per seated source) has nothing to act on here; the tab is spine-only and the brief's longest sections were inapplicable.

Nearly every pool's fields read 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD', while the rule states a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it in its own word. That makes a lawful second sentence effectively impossible in most pools, so I wrote one sentence throughout; it is unclear whether one-sentence spines are the intent or a degenerate outcome.

Several corpus lines break bars they are given under: MARKET-OPEN states an origin (a founding-as-record, explicitly refused), three spines use semicolons and one a colon, and the foodSecurity line's closing 'which it is not in a comfortable town' contradicts the page's own prosperity badge 'Comfortable' and is also a which-clause close. I kept each claim and dropped the breach, but the instruction 'the claim you must keep' is hard to honour when the claim itself is the barred element.

Two pools on one page pull opposite ways with no guidance: DS-GEN-5 'ordinary' claims the town takes very little from the road, DS-GEN-6 'road' claims the road is a condition of the town's existence. I wrote them as through-traffic versus inbound supply so they can stand together, but the reconciliation was mine to invent.

Two smaller gaps. The stance words used here (elder, unfolding, counterforce, 'ledger · marks deficit') are never defined in the brief, which names only ledger/street/visitor. And the scores.magical WEAK claim ('no arrangement for magic') sits against the page's own arrival scene (a magelight lamp post at the gate) and the card's Alchemist shop, with no statement of whether that counts as a contradicted page line.

Seats with no roster: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War' face 0 is seated on `elders` and the two DS-DEF-2 faces seated on `garrison` have no entry under the town's `roles`/`sources`. I followed the 'copy the corpus verbatim at that seat' rule. For `elders` that forces a contradiction: the corpus row still carries unfilled `{elders}` and `{v:take}` tokens, and the pool declares no slots, so a verbatim copy prints raw identifiers, which the mechanical bars forbid. No rule says which one wins.

Slot declarations disagree with themselves in 'Invasion & War': the pool says 'slots you may use: (none)' and then declares a `{court}` fill. I wrote a court role in plain words and used no token. Also unclear whether a declared fill must be spent or may be skipped for {settlement}; I read it as optional and named the town in one unit only, to respect the once-per-page opening rule.

The brief's attribution guidance is self-contradictory on one frame: 'one of the aldermen has it that' is offered as licensed syntax variation while 'has it that' is listed among the mannered frames ruling 42 struck. I avoided the frame entirely.

'The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields' is ambiguous against the three-sentence unit cap, since a rendered unit is spine plus a drawn face. I kept nearly every spine and face to one sentence so no combination exceeds three, which may under-use the licence.

Two roster roles collide with ruling 42c's plain-word bar: the stranger roster seats 'a pedlar' and the register roster 'the high priest' / class language the bar rewrites. I avoided 'pedlar'. Also, 'granary' is an institution row name but a barred word, so I wrote 'grain store' throughout.

The brief's SHAPE section says the spine is ALWAYS bare, on the document's own authority, while the VOICE section says a spine may instead be carried by the public or a source and that a pool's three spines take three different shapes. The turn then gives each pool a stance (visitor, street, counterforce, unfolding) that reads like a carrier instruction. I wrote every spine bare, since bare never breaks a bar, but which of the two governs is genuinely unclear.

The stance values in the turn (unfolding, visitor, street, counterforce) are never defined anywhere in the brief; only three stances ([ledger], [street], [visitor]) are described, and 'unfolding' and 'counterforce' appear nowhere. I could not tell whether they change anything about the line I was to write.

Pool 'riskLabel: Holding' declares {seat} and {faction} with the SAME fill ('Guild Council'), so the corpus line's claim ('the seat holds because the faction is still the heavier of the two') collapses into a tautology when rendered. I wrote around it by keeping the weight claim without the two-party framing, but the card gives no second party to name.

The brief says to write ONE sentence where no fields are recorded, but also to name the town at most once per unit and never as the first word of two units on a page, with no guidance on how often the settlement fill should be spent across the nine units of one page. I named it twice and left the slot unused elsewhere on the strength of 'or none at all'.

Two page lines coexist uneasily for the reader: the badge says stability Stable while the machine line describes a live guild-versus-merchant quarrel, and the pool 'stable matched' asks for a line about one reliable answer a stranger can plan on. The two-ladders paragraph covers badge-versus-band, not badge-versus-recentConflict, so I kept both claims narrow and let them stand side by side.

DS-GEN-5 'ordinary (route road and the default)' and DS-GEN-6 'road' ship on the same page with directly opposing claims about the town's road dependency, and brief.md gives no reconciliation rule for two competing pools shipped together (unlike its explicit rule for the readiness badge vs band).

The scores.magical: WEAK corpus fallback line ('keeps no arrangement for the Art') looks like a field-denial under the brief's own refusal rule, since town.md's armedForces.arcane lists an Alchemist shop as an arcane asset — the shipped fallback appears to violate the bar it would enforce on a written face.

brief.md never states outright that a colon is barred on the fair copy/spine; that is only inferable from Part V listing the colon as a notebook device 'licensed on dm-only faces only.' Three of the given corpus fallback lines on this page use a colon, so their legality on the spine is implicit rather than stated.

Several pools carry a 'stance' tag (elder, unfolding, counterforce) that brief.md never defines, outside the three stances it actually names (ledger/street/visitor); since spine is always 'bare' regardless of stance, it is unclear what these tags should change about a spine-only unit.

The instruction that a unit's second sentence 'must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is hard to reconcile with fields marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD ('assert no value for this field beyond what the key says') on most of these pools; I defaulted to one-sentence spines wherever the only listed field was unreadable rather than risk an unlawful assertion.

Two faces were assigned to sources the town card does not seat: DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' face 0 is specified as speaking through `elders`, and both DS-DEF-2 'Internal Security' face 5 and DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival: STRONG' face 1 are specified as `garrison` -- but town.md's `roles`/`sources` arrays list only court, gate, guild, hall, market, public, register, stranger, tavern, watch (no elders or garrison entry), and forceBuckets.garrison is explicitly false. Per the brief's 'WHEN THE CARD GIVES A FACE NOTHING TO STAND ON, COPY THE CORPUS' rule I copied those three corpus faces verbatim rather than inventing an unseated role.

The verbatim corpus fallback for the elders face ('{elders} {v:take} the walls for their own boundary...') is itself unrendered template syntax (curly-brace role/verb tokens), unlike every other corpus face in the turn which is already plain prose. 'Copy verbatim' is ambiguous here: I reproduced the raw token text as given rather than inventing a rendering the card gives no basis for.

DS-DEF-2 'Invasion & War: walls with NO force' lists 'slots you may use: (none)' but then supplies a `{court}` fill ('A woman who brought a matter to the court') directly beneath that header, which only makes sense as a slot fill. I treated the explicit fill as authoritative for face 2's attribution and note the 'slots: (none)' header as contradictory.

DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival: STRONG' seats the `hall` source at both face 2 and face 6 on the same page/pool, which runs against the exemplar pack's own (non-binding, taste-level) guidance that 'the same role never speaks twice on one page.' Since the card's face seating is stated as already decided, I wrote both, varying the attribution's surface form (an institutional idiom vs. a named roster entry) rather than omitting either.

The corpus fallback for DS-DEF-5 'arcane defense PRESENT' uses a colon, but PART V of the brief states the colon is a notebook-only device absent from the fair copy; I rewrote that spine without a colon rather than imitating the corpus line's own breach, per the brief's explicit instruction not to imitate a corpus breach.

Pool STALLED declares {institution} as "Cartographer's guild", but the town block's institution rows list "Cartographer's workshop" and no cartographers' guild; the card's fill was written as instructed, and it names a body the town block does not carry.

"The second sentence of a unit must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word" is unsatisfiable where every listed field reads UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (C3, POSTURE, STALLED), so those spines were written as one sentence; POSTURE kept the corpus's two-sentence shape because the corpus claim itself is two sentences.

The STALLED corpus fallback uses a semicolon, which the mechanical bars forbid outright; the brief says not to imitate a breach, so the claim was recut onto a comma join, but it is unclear whether a fallback that would itself be dropped still counts as the shipping line.

Every pool lists a stance (visitor, ledger, street) yet gives zero faces, and the brief makes the spine a bare fact in the archiver's own hand; the stance survives only as a tag, so it could not be carried in voice, and the guidance on what a stance does to a faceless unit is missing.

The INCOME MIX corpus claim is "well past half", a proportion, while the refusal list bars a rate stated as record and the bars bar digits; "most" was used to keep the claim without the rate. The four income rows are never enumerated, so the carrying trade cannot be named.

DS-POW-4 riskLabel:Holding fills both {seat} and {faction} to the identical value "Guild Council" on this town, so the corpus's two-party comparison ("holds because {faction} is heavier") collapses into one institution being weighed against itself; unclear whether that is intended or a degenerate card-fill case.

DS-POW-4 legitimacyHold's listed field is a raw JS ternary/property-access expression (power.publicLegitimacy ... govMultiplier) rather than a plain field name, and is marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD; unclear whether a second sentence naming the general topic with no value actually satisfies 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields.'

DS-POW-5 'mixed' offers no settlement slot at all, unlike its sibling pool 'governing body name' in the same block, even though the 'mixed' pool's own corpus-line fallback uses {settlement}; the asymmetry between the two isn't explained.

Several pools carry stance tags ('unfolding', 'counterforce') that brief.md never defines; only three named stances (ledger/street/visitor) are spelled out, so it's unclear what register distinction, if any, the newer tags require beyond the blanket rule that a spine is always bare.

The shipped corpus-line fallback for DS-POW-2 'recentConflict present' itself contains a semicolon ('explained to them; it is recent enough'), which the mechanical bars forbid outright; brief.md says not to imitate a corpus breach but does not say what should happen when the fallback that ships on refusal is itself unlawful under the current rules.

Most seats in the four DS-DEF-2 pools name sources the town block does not roster at all (watch, court, guild, hall, gate, muster, garrison). The turn still says each 'is one of the roles the town block lists for X under roles, and no other' — an instruction with an empty option set. I fell back to the brief's 'WHEN THE CARD GIVES A FACE NOTHING TO STAND ON, COPY THE CORPUS' rule and copied those 11 corpus faces verbatim, but the turn never says that is the intended reading, and the two rules point opposite ways.

The corpus faces I was told to copy verbatim breach bars the brief calls hard drops: the watch/court/guild/hall/gate/muster/garrison rows speak through unseated roles, and the Invasion spine's corpus wording uses 'week', which the mechanical bars list among the engine spellings. The brief says a copied corpus row is never refused, so I copied them, but a literal tier-0 pass would red them.

The 'First-Survey qualification' pool's whole claim is the document describing its own coverage, which ruling 40 and the E2 ratchet bar on a player face ('the survey', 'the record', 'this office'). I wrote it as 'the safety reading here is a first look' to keep the claim without a barred phrase, but whether that pool is writable at all under ruling 40 is genuinely unclear.

'structure null (nothing organized recognized)' sits against an institutions row for an 'Underground network', and the brief's own refusal list names "'nothing organised behind it' where the town's own rows list a street gang" as a refusal. I wrote only that a stranger asking gets incomprehension, asserting nothing about whether anything exists, but the pool key and the row are in tension.

Seven pools declare the settlement slot and the brief says both to write the fill and that using none at all is allowed, while also barring the town as the first word of two units. With no guidance on how many units on a page should name it, I named Hochhausen in three of thirteen; that number is a guess. Separately, audience is dm but every pool says 'notebook: none', so no notebook row was written anywhere and the dm register went unused.

The STALLED pool's slot fill names the institution "Cartographer's guild," but the town block's own institutions list only carries "Cartographer's workshop" (no guild entry) -- the two source files disagree on this body's name.

For fields marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD (prosperityRank, exportPosture.status, and all four STALLED readings), the brief says both "assert no value beyond what the key says" and, for a second sentence, "name it in its own word" -- it's not fully spelled out how much descriptive latitude beyond the bare key phrase that second clause is allowed.

The STALLED pool's own corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which the mechanical bars forbid; the brief says not to imitate a corpus breach but doesn't say whether the rest of that sentence is still safe to draw on once it's known to break a bar.

Whether spelled-out number words (not just digit characters) count as barred by "no digit" is not stated explicitly; several pools carry exact frozen row counts that a professional archiver's hand might otherwise render in words.

The notebook section calls the colon one of "the notebook's devices... which the fair copy does not have," but the top mechanical-bars list never names the colon outright -- and the DS-ECO-1 corpus line itself uses one -- so it's ambiguous whether a colon on the fair-copy page is a hard violation or only a notebook convention.

Audience is dm, and the brief spends a whole part (PART V) on the notebook register, but every one of the nine pools says notebook: none. The DM register was unusable on this page; the dm/player distinction made no difference to anything written.

The two omitted pools still print a full slot table, a move order, a corpus line and a notebook instruction beneath the OMIT directive. The directive and the writing instructions read as contradictory until you notice OMIT wins; a reader working top-down could easily start drafting.

The {seat} fill is 'Elected Reeve' and the institution row is 'Village reeve', but ruling 42c names 'the reeve' outright as a word that does not survive the withdrawn archaism licence. Whether an engine fill overrides 42c is not stated anywhere; I treated the fill as the page's own printed words and used it.

The slot is named 'seat' while a mechanical bar forbids 'schema word, raw identifier'. It is unclear whether the ordinary English word 'seat' may appear in prose at all, so I wrote around it everywhere. The same doubt hit 'weekly' in 'Weekly market' against the 'no week' bar.

Several pools say 'THE FIELDS this pool reads: none are recorded, so write ONE sentence and no second', yet their corpus lines (Tolerated, mixed) are two sentences. The fallback that ships breaks the instruction given for the replacement, and the brief says not to imitate a corpus breach, so I wrote one sentence and dropped the corpus's second.

Eight face-slots across the DS-DEF-2 pools (watch, court, guild, hall in the Invasion&War pool; gate, muster in Internal Security; gate, muster, watch, garrison in Economic Survival) are told to speak through a role "the town block lists ... under roles", but town.md's roles array only carries rosters for elders, market, public, register, stranger and tavern - there is no watch/court/guild/hall/gate/muster/garrison entry at all, and forceBuckets even marks watch/militia/garrison false. Since no lawful town-specific role phrase exists for those, I copied the pool's own corpus line verbatim at each of those seats per brief.md's 'nothing to stand on, copy the corpus' rule rather than invent an unseated role.

Pool "capture none" (DS-DEF-4) is explicitly marked in turn.md as 'NOT WRITEABLE ON THIS TOWN: OMIT IT ... Return no unit for this pool,' which conflicts with the outer instruction to produce one unit per pool the turn lists. I followed the turn's own per-pool instruction and omitted it, so 13 units were written for the 14 pools listed.

The DS-DEF-11 'UNWALLED-SMALL' corpus fallback line contains a semicolon, which the mechanical bars forbid outright and which brief.md says explicitly not to imitate even from the corpus; I wrote a fresh, semicolon-free spine instead of the given fallback.

town.md sets "compromisedRate": 0.7 but "compromised": [] and no field in any of these pools flags a specific source as compromised, so the ruling-26 concealment/reassurance mechanic in the brief was never actually invoked despite that fairly high compromised-rate number sitting on the card unused.

turn.md declares audience "dm" at the top, but every single pool's line reads 'notebook: none. Return an empty list,' so the DM notebook register the brief spends its whole PART V describing is never exercised anywhere on this page - worth confirming that's the intended state for this town/tab rather than a mismatch.
Audience is 'dm', but all 18 pools say 'notebook: none. Return an empty list.' The DM register the brief spends PART V on is unreachable on this page, so the dm/player distinction buys nothing here.

Almost every pool's fields read 'UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD', and the rule 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' then makes any second sentence unwritable. That silently forces every unit to one sentence; the brief never says so.

GARRISONED (DS-GEN-17) is the sharpest conflict: its corpus claim says the town keeps paid professionals for safety, but the town block has forceBuckets garrison/militia/watch all false and armedForces.standing/contracted empty. Only a charter hall and a veteran's lodge exist. Unclear whether keeping that claim is lawful or whether the pool should be omitted.

The two DS-REL-2 pools carry claims that read against one another on the same page (one tie weighs more than the rest, vs the ties here are wholly ordinary with nothing further to say). No guidance on writing both in one render.

Several corpus fallback lines breach the mechanical bars they are given under (semicolons in GARRISONED and scores.monster, 'will and will not' in prominentRelationship, a counted 'second day' in intensity: low). The brief says not to imitate the breach, but the claim to be kept is only stated in the refused form, and 'faces to write: 0' on all 18 pools leaves the roles roster, pairs, compromised roll, public and observed face entirely unused.

Two of the nine listed pools (block DS-POW-2 'governing faction holds a NARROW plurality' vid 2, and block DS-POW-7 'layer DORMANT (no ledger materialized)' vid 2) were explicitly marked NOT WRITEABLE / OMIT by the turn itself, so no unit was produced for them and unitsWritten is 7 of 9 — assumed the correct reading is to simply leave them out of the array rather than emit any placeholder.

This town's role roster carries no 'hall' source (sources: elders, market, public, register, stranger, tavern only, no hall/mayor), yet the shipped corpus fallback lines for two of these DS-POW pools use 'the hall' generically for the seat of power; it was unclear whether that generic usage is licensed on a town with no seated hall role, so I avoided the word and used non-role phrasing ('the seat', 'the governing body') instead.

Several pools state 'THE FIELDS this pool reads: none are recorded, so write ONE sentence and no second,' while their own corpus fallback spine runs two sentences carrying two parts of one claim; it wasn't fully specified how much of that second-sentence content should survive when compressed into a single sentence versus be dropped.

For 'riskLabel: Holding' the pool's slot list is 'settlement' only, even though the seat/faction body (Elected Reeve) is otherwise nameable from the town block and appears in the corpus line's implicit referent; unclear whether the slot list is a hard ban on naming that body in this unit or only limits which curly-brace fill tokens resolve.

The stance tag 'counterforce' on the Tolerated pool is never defined among the brief's three named stance families (ledger/street/visitor), so its intended construction beyond 'state the bare fact' was unspecified.

The 'threshold' stance on the foodSecurity pool is never defined anywhere in brief.md; only ledger/street/visitor are given as the three named families, so its register had to be guessed as a neutral variant.

Several of the card's own CORPUS LINE fallbacks breach the mechanical bars they exist to enforce (a semicolon in GARRISONED's and scores.monster's corpus spine, a which-clause closer in foodSecurity's, and the literal word 'will' in prominentRelationship's 'what the town will and will not do') -- the brief anticipates this ('do not imitate the breach') but does not flag that the fallback itself would fail its own tier-0 refuter if a unit were omitted and the corpus line shipped as-is.

GARRISONED's field (readings.inst) is UNREADABLE while the town's own forceBuckets (garrison/militia/watch) are all false and only an adventurers' charter hall exists under armedForces -- nothing on the card explains what specifically makes the GARRISONED key true, so the spine had to stay generic ('armed order,' 'professionals') to avoid asserting a denied value.

It is not spelled out whether a possessive use of the settlement fill ("Hochhausen's") counts toward the 'name the town at most once per unit' cap and the 'never as the first word of two units on one page' rule, or only a bare nominative use does; this response treated a possessive as one full naming.

For pools where every listed field is UNREADABLE, it's ambiguous how a permitted second sentence could ever 'rest on' and 'name' that field 'in its own word' without asserting a value the card withholds -- the corpus examples (e.g. intensity: low) only gesture at the field's topic indirectly, which this response followed as the safest reading.

The town's role roster seats 'a pedlar' and 'a guild factor', both of which the brief's ruling 42c strikes as archaisms ('a travelling trader not a pedlar', 'a guild member not a factor'); the seating and the word ban contradict each other, so I used neither role.

The pool key 'INCOME MIX: two or three sources between them' sits against economicState.incomeSources.length = 10 on the same card. I wrote to the key but hedged it ('most of what the town lives on'), since a bare 'two or three' would read as denying the ten rows.

The rule 'the second sentence must rest on one of these fields and name it in its own word' is unsatisfiable on three pools (DS-ECO-1, DS-ECO-10, DS-GEN-18) where every listed field is UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD; I rested those second sentences on the pool key itself.

Several corpus fallback lines breach bars the brief says not to imitate: a colon (DS-ECO-1), a semicolon (DS-GEN-18), a future indicative plus a direct address to the reader ('you will be given', DS-ECO-12), and a two-sentence spine on DS-ECO-9 where the card instructs one sentence and no second. Unclear whether keeping the claim while dropping the breach is what the harness scores.

The page is audience dm, yet every pool says 'notebook: none' and the one dm-only pool carries its note in `spine`, so all seven notebook lists are empty and the DM page has no private rows. Also unclear: each pool prints a stance tag (visitor/street/ledger) while the brief says the spine is the archiver's bare fact by default, so whether a stance obliges a source-carried spine is left to judgment (I mixed bare and source-carried).

Two seats had no role to stand on: DS-DEF-2 'Beasts & Monsters' face 10 asks for `elders` and DS-DEF-2 'Economic Survival' face 2 asks for `archiver`, but the town block's `roles` list carries neither source (only court, garrison, gate, guild, hall, market, public, register, stranger, tavern, watch). I applied the brief's 'copy the corpus verbatim at that seat' rule for both.

The brief's own attribution-variation list offers 'one of the aldermen has it that' as an approved syntax, while the same paragraph says ruling 42 struck 'has it that' as a mannered frame. I avoided the phrase entirely.

Several roster role phrases collide with the archaism ban of ruling 42c: the guild roster's 'a guild factor' contains the barred word 'factor', the stranger roster's 'a pedlar' is barred by name, and 'a serjeant …' is a dated spelling of uncertain standing. I avoided 'factor' and 'pedlar' and used 'a serjeant on the wall' once, flagging the doubt.

DS-DEF-3 'First-Survey qualification' asks for a pool whose whole claim is that the reading is a first look, which runs against ruling 40's bar on the fair copy referring to itself ('the survey', 'the record', 'this office'). I carried the claim as a passive 'is reckoned on a first look' without naming the document; the pool may simply be unwriteable under 40.

Pools 'Internal Security' and 'structure organized' declare `settlement` as a usable slot but print no fill line for it (unlike the others, which give '{settlement} is "Rundgate"'). I wrote 'the town' rather than guess, and used the name in only two units on the page, neither of them twice and only one at the head of a sentence.

Every pool lists its read fields as UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD while also saying a second sentence must rest on one of those fields and name it in its own word. That makes any second sentence unwritable, so all fifteen spines are one sentence; the brief's licence for a two-sentence spine is unreachable on this page.
Pool 'economicViability.viable: true' declares the settlement slot twice with conflicting fills ('Rundgate' and 'R'). Nothing says which wins, so the slot was left unused there.

The turn says audience dm, but every pool says notebook none / return an empty list, so the dm page carries no private rows at all. The brief's whole PART V register had nothing to act on, and 'faces to write: 0' on all fifteen pools likewise idled the source, role, pair and compromised machinery that most of the brief is about.

The brief bars naming the badge word, but one pool key IS the badge word ('defenseProfile.readiness.label: Well-Defended') and the same word is printed as a badge on the page beside it. Wrote to the state without naming it, which is the only reading available.

Several constraints are stated per rendered PAGE (one physical particular, name the town at most once and never opening two units, no repeated first three words) while the turn hands fifteen pools on one page each declaring a settlement slot. Treated the whole turn as one page: the town is named once and nowhere twice, though whether these pools truly share a page is not stated.

Turn.md's header line says 'THE LINES TO WRITE' but lists seven pools, not the six the task instructions implied — I wrote one unit per pool listed (7 total), trusting turn.md as authoritative per rule 1.

For SECURE (DS-ECO-9) the card says 'no fields are recorded, so write ONE sentence and no second,' but the corpus fallback given for that same pool is two sentences — a direct contradiction between the instruction and its own fallback; I followed the explicit one-sentence instruction over the fallback's shape.

The corpus fallback for DS-ECO-1/vid1 and DS-GEN-18/vid2 both contain mechanical-bar violations (a colon and a semicolon respectively) inside lines the brief calls 'the claim you must keep... where it breaks a bar above, do not imitate the breach' — so the fallback text itself would be refused by the tier-0 refuter if it shipped as-is, which is internally inconsistent for a designated fallback.

For TIER: minor shadow activity (DS-ECO-6), the only field given is a raw number (blackMarketCapture = 8, FROZEN), but floor 2 and the mechanical bars forbid any digit or count on the page — the card supplies a field it then forbids me from ever stating, so the pool can only be written by ignoring the one field it names.

Two of the ten fallback corpus lines contain semicolons (pools 'Approved' and 'stable matched', among others), which the brief's own mechanical bar forbids outright — the given fallback is not itself lawful under the bars it is supposed to exemplify, so I paraphrased around the semicolon rather than keeping the corpus wording.

Pools 'council' and 'riskLabel: Holding' instruct 'write ONE sentence and no second' but their given corpus fallback lines are two sentences each — there is a direct tension between 'keep the corpus line's claim' and the one-sentence cap; I condensed both clauses into a single sentence.

turn.md uses stance tags 'threshold' and 'unfolding' for two pools, but brief.md defines only three stances (ledger/street/visitor) as 'THE THREE OLD STANCES' — no guidance exists for what register these two additional stance words should produce on a spine with zero faces.

For 'legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold' the only field the pool reads is marked UNREADABLE BY THIS CARD, yet the instructions still say a second sentence 'must rest on one of these fields... or the instruments withhold it' — it is unclear whether any second sentence is actually writable here without asserting a value the card withholds, so I wrote one sentence only.

THE ORDER (e.g. V5 'INSTITUTION then PRESENT') is asserted as a constraint the spine must realise but is never defined precisely — whether it governs literal word order, grammatical subject placement, or only content sequencing is left to inference from the corpus line's own shape.

Two faces named a source this city-tier town does not seat as a roster role: Beasts & Monsters face 10 asks for 'elders' and Economic Survival face 2 asks for 'archiver', but town.md's roles/sources lists (11 entries) contain neither, and the brief itself says elders exist only 'below town' tier. The corpus line handed to the writer for that pool is thus flagged by the same brief as unlawful -- I kept the underlying claim but did not imitate that construction, per the brief's own 'do not imitate the breach' instruction.

Several other corpus fallback lines given in turn.md break the current mechanical bars they are meant to exemplify (semicolons in the walls/garrison/mercenary/WALLED-STRAINED/Logistics corpus spines, a colon in the Moderate/garrison spines, a Not-X-but-Y construction in 'structure organized'), consistent with the brief's warning that the corpus 'is not a model of the law' -- noted since a less careful pass could read the fallback text as a style template rather than a claim-only fallback.

Several pools list a single FROZEN/LIVE field for grounding a second sentence (e.g. readiness score, economic score) but the pool key already states the band in words, so the 'name it in its own word' instruction and the pool key convey the same information; I treated the field as satisfied by naming the band's qualitative sense (e.g. 'reads strong') rather than inventing new numeric-adjacent language, but the exact bar for what counts as 'resting on' a bare score field versus the pool key itself is not fully spelled out.

Per its explicit instruction, DS-DEF-4 pool 'capture adversarial' (vid 2) was omitted entirely -- no unit was written for it -- since the turn states outright that nothing in the card licenses a sentence for it and that the hand corpus should draw it.
